# Matriarch Firmware Fixes

> Unofficial bug fixes for the Moog Matriarch analog synthesizer's firmware v1.3.0, the last release before the Matriarch was discontinued. A free browser tool patches the user's own copy of Moog's firmware file locally, nothing is uploaded. The first fix makes released notes stop when the key is let go in paraphonic mode, so staccato playing works again. Free software under the GPLv3 or later, by Benjamin Dehli for Dehli Musikk. Not affiliated with Moog Music.

In 2- and 4-note paraphonic mode, firmware v1.3.0 keeps a released note's oscillator sounding for 125 ms while other keys are held. Moog lists it as the known issue "Paraphonic Mixer Gate Length". The patcher changes that hold to 5 ms (recommended), 50 ms (how firmware v1.1.0 behaved) or any whole number of milliseconds from 0 to 125.

## Pages

- [Matriarch Firmware Patcher](https://benjamindehli.github.io/matriarch-firmware-fixes/index.html.md): the patcher, what the fix does and why, the hold time in each firmware version, Moog's other known issues, and common questions.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/benjamindehli/matriarch-firmware-fixes): the patcher, a command-line version in Python, tests and analysis tools, GPLv3 or later.
- [README](https://github.com/benjamindehli/matriarch-firmware-fixes/blob/main/README.md): how to patch and flash, how the fix works at instruction level, the firmware file format, and hardware notes.
- [Releases](https://github.com/benjamindehli/matriarch-firmware-fixes/releases): release notes for each version.

## Facts

- Supported firmware: Moog Matriarch v1.3.0 only (`Matriarch_Firmware_v1_3_0.syx`). Other versions are refused.
- Fixed: Paraphonic Mixer Gate Length. Tested on hardware with 5 ms and 50 ms.
- Not fixed yet: Send Program Change, Arp sending Sustain CC while Hold is active, Load Default Settings leaving global mode stuck, Sequence Random Repeat, Sequence Keyed Restart, Keyed Timing Reset with Hold, Delay Sync CV Bend stepping.
- The patched firmware isn't distributed, because it's still Moog's copyrighted firmware. Users patch their own copy.
- Flashing uses Moog's normal procedure with a SysEx tool: INVALIDATE, re-select the MIDI port, ERASE, then the patched file. Flashing Moog's original file the same way restores stock firmware.
- The patch doesn't touch Multi Trig or the envelope retrigger timing that fixed stuck envelopes.
